calculateDate.description:
Calculate a date variable for use in comparing to other date variables.

For example, a date may be retrieved from an LDAP directory that needs to be compared to a date in the future.  Thus you create a date in the future with this action, then compare the two date variables in the Assert Date action.

REFERENCE: LDAP Dates are in the form YYYYMMDDHHMMSS followed by Z (for Zulu time), or +|-HHMM.  Where HH is the number of hours and minutes plus or minus Zulu time.  E.g. 20141201031430-0500 is 5 hours behind Zulu time which is US Eastern Standard Time

desc.html:
Usage

This connector provides a Web Service listener. Actions are provided to start and stop the listener as well as configure extended endpoint properties. Once the listener has been started, any POST or PUT to any endpoint will create a GET endpoint with that same URL in the listener. This GET endpoint will return the data that was provided in the POST or PUT. In this manner, you can validate the data posted to the listener. Use the HTTP Connector to perform the GET and validate the data.

For example: POST on http://server:port/myendpoint with a JSON payload, will create a GET endpoint of /myendpoint that will return the same JSON payload provided by the POST. Use the HTTP connector to perform the GET on http://localhost:port/myendpoint and validate the data.

Using the Configuration action, you can set additional endpoint properties such as return data for subsequent POST/PUT or GET requests, Basic Auth, content type of the return data, and return codes. This additional configuration is optional. Hover over any label in this action for assistance.

If the client performs a DELETE on an endpoint, that endpoint will be removed.

Once the listener has been stopped, all endpoints are removed.



Static Endpoints
  • Test Connection: GET http://server:port/wsconntest
  • Shutdown listener: GET http://server:port/shutdown
  • List Configured Endpoints: GET http://server:port/wslist
